name: A Fort Smith street

place_source.title: Wikidata: Fort Smith (Q79535), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A block of front gardens in the Arkansas Valley between the Ozarks and the Ouachitas: redbud and dogwood under street maple and hackberry, magnolia and holly holding green through the winter, a fox squirrel in the oaks, a striped skunk coming through the service alley after dark and a big brown bat working the street lamps at dusk.

facts.text: Fort Smith has a humid subtropical climate with generally mild winters and hot, humid summers.

source.title: Wikipedia: Fort Smith, Arkansas
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Fort Smith, Arkansas", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The monthly mean temperature in Fort Smith ranges from 40.4 F in January to 83.1 F in July, with 77.8 days a year reaching 90 F and 11.1 days reaching 100 F.

source.title: Wikipedia: Fort Smith, Arkansas
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Fort Smith, Arkansas", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Fort Smith lies on the Arkansas-Oklahoma state border, in the Arkansas Valley at the confluence of the Arkansas and Poteau rivers, strategically located between the Ozarks to the north and the Ouachita Mountains to the south.

source.title: Wikipedia: Fort Smith, Arkansas
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Fort Smith, Arkansas", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Arkansas is in the Central Time Zone, which is the America/Chicago time zone, and Fort Smith is in the Central Time Zone.
As of the 2020 census, Fort Smith was the third-most populous city in Arkansas, with a population of 89,142.

source.title: Wikipedia: Fort Smith, Arkansas
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Fort Smith, Arkansas", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Fort Smith is situated near an area known as Tornado Alley, and the city has been struck by three major tornadoes, in 1898, 1927 and 1996.

source.title: Wikipedia: Fort Smith, Arkansas
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Fort Smith, Arkansas", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: American robins are the most abundant landbird in North America, with 370 million individuals, and forage on lawns for earthworms.

source.title: Wikipedia: American robin
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "American robin", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The scissor-tailed flycatcher breeds in open shrubby country in Arkansas, Oklahoma, Texas, Kansas, Louisiana and Missouri, and winters from southern Mexico to Panama; it is Oklahoma's state bird.

source.title: Wikipedia: Scissor-tailed flycatcher
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Scissor-tailed flycatcher", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Fox squirrels are most abundant in open forest stands with little understory vegetation, are often found in urban neighborhoods with trees, and will nest in an attic as readily as a hollow tree.

source.title: Wikipedia: Fox squirrel
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Fox squirrel", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Big brown bats roost in mines, caves, tunnels, buildings, bat boxes, tree cavities, storm drains, wood piles and rock crevices, and forage in cities around street lamps.

source.title: Wikipedia: Big brown bat
